piece.title: String Quartet No.12 in F major, Op.96 (“American”)
piece.why: The famous viola opening: the theme starts in the viola under violin tremolo, moves to Violin I, then trades between cello and Violin I and cascades up through all four parts.

roster.label: Church brass: 2 trumpets (one beginner), horn, euphonium

plan.summary: The tune moves around the quartet. The viola has it in bars 1–8, first violin takes over in 9–16, and the viola leads again in 17–20 with first violin imitating it. Trumpet 1 follows the tune the whole way. In bars 7–8 it drops back to the viola's written octave, where the viola is the lowest line, so the accompaniment stays above it as in the original. The euphonium holds the cello bass, the horn covers the first-violin figures and the viola's inner line, and the beginner trumpet gets the simple second-violin patterns.

assignments.reason: The viola has the opening tune. Up an octave it sits well for trumpet and comes through clearly.
The viola becomes the lowest voice here, so trumpet 1 plays it at written pitch. That keeps the horn and trumpet 2 figures above it, as in the original.
The tune moves to first violin. Down an octave, trumpet 1 keeps playing it with no break.
Bar 16 closes the first-violin phrase low, so trumpet 1 plays it at written pitch to stay above F3.
The viola leads again in the closing phrase, so trumpet 1 stays on the tune. Only the opening D3 moves up an octave.
These are the first violin's rocking F–A figures. Down an octave they give the horn a warm, blended background.
The violin's high arpeggio goes down two octaves so the horn stays under C5. It still sits above the viola tune in trumpet 1.
Back to one octave down to finish the phrase.
The viola's inner line, mostly stepwise, fits the horn's middle range as written and fills in the harmony under the tune.
First violin echoes the viola's tune. At written pitch it stays in the horn's range and above the viola line in bar 19.
The final climb goes down an octave so it fits the horn.
Second violin's simple A–C figures, down an octave so the beginner stays below B-flat.
The A–F figures fit as written.
Alternating A–F figures sit comfortably for a beginner, as written.
Repeated D4 eighth notes, an easy pulse part for a beginner.
The cello bass fits the euphonium's F2–F4 range and stays at the bottom. Only the low D2 in bar 9 moves up an octave.

dropped.reason: The scale climbs to C5, above the beginner trumpet's top note, and every other player is busy. The horn's viola line covers this harmony.
These fast runs climb to A5, too high and too quick for the beginner trumpet. The tune, bass and viola line still give full harmony.
The second violin's arpeggio climbs to D6, far above the beginner's range. The tune, the horn's imitation and the bass carry the ending.
